summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, heart failure (LVEF 30%), type 2 diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for evaluation of anemia and melena. The bleeding was attributed to gastric ulceration caused by concurrent ibuprofen and warfarin use. He became transiently hypotensive but declined blood transfusion, so he was managed with IV fluids, vitamin K, and prothrombin complex concentrate. An EGD confirmed diffuse gastric ulceration without active bleeding, and pantoprazole was started. His warfarin was held and later restarted. MRI revealed lumbar stenosis causing his chronic leg pain, and he was started on acetaminophen and oxycodone for pain, with referral to a spine surgeon. He had runs of NSVT during admission and declined ICD placement despite counseling. He was also treated for bilateral conjunctivitis and found to have trace vitreous hemorrhage in the left eye, with outpatient ophthalmology follow-up arranged. He was discharged home in stable condition with a stable hemoglobin, instructions to avoid NSAIDs, and plans for follow-up with cardiology, spine surgery, and his PCP.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Gastric ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation
Adverse effect of anticoagulants, initial encounter
Adverse effect of propionic acid derivatives, initial encounter
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with unspecified diabetic retinopathy without macular edema
